html:
A Japanese film of 1954 directed by Akira Kurosawa. A village of poor farmers hires seven masterless samurai to defend it against bandits who will come to steal their harvest. Toshiro Mifune plays Kikuchiyo, a wild farmer's son pretending to be a samurai.

The story is set in 1586, near the end of the Sengoku period, when Japan was torn by civil wars before the Tokugawa peace. It runs over three hours and was costly for its time. Kurosawa shot the final battle in mud and pouring rain.

Its pattern of gathering a team, preparing a defence and a last fight became a model for action films everywhere. Hollywood remade it as the western The Magnificent Seven in 1960, and its influence runs through later war, heist and space films from the American film industry. With Kurosawa's Rashomon before it, it made Japanese cinema famous abroad.
